correctness.rationale: For every regular Euclidean Platonic solid the equal-face-area Cauchy formula yields Y=2/m sum_i |U·normal_i|. Gaussian radial/angular independence gives the exact spherical two-normal product kernel (2/(3π))[sqrt(1-t²)+t asin t]. Expanding E Y² produces 8/(3πm²) sum_ij F(|normal_i·normal_j|)-1. Explicit exact normal families comprise m=4,6,8,12,20 and all m² ordered correlations: tetra {1:4,1/3:12}; cube {1:12,0:24}; octa {1:16,1/3:48}; dodeca {1:24,1/sqrt5:120}; icosa {1:40,1/3:240,sqrt5/3:120}. Substitution proves all four displayed V formulas; strict order follows from disjoint high-precision intervals and is compatible with source rational-interval method. Since mean area S/4, independence gives exact relative RMS sqrt(V/k), so k=ceil(10000 V) = (104,57,57,16,6). Numerical finite experiments are corroborative only. Edge-length similarity cancels; no claim for adaptive/uniform-confidence or non-Platonic bodies.
residual_risks: Independent numerical recomputation and exact arithmetic in source establish listed finite correlations but do not claim a formal proof assistant run.
Simulated 40000 views and numerical quadrature cannot prove strict inequalities; finite correlation classifications plus elementary analytic kernel are proof basis.

originality.rationale: The complete five-solid exact relative-variance classification is not entailed by the inspected prior literature: its cube, regular tetrahedron and regular octahedron values ARE already exact second-moment evaluations in Finch (2012), after explicit scale and mean normalization, and the tetrahedron–octahedron equality is independently known from the projection-body equivalence. These are prior-covered components, not novel entries. The dodecahedron and icosahedron absolute-normal correlation rows and exact variance evaluations, their positions in the complete sharp ranking, and their uniform-view RMS sample counts were not found in the inspected primary full texts, catalogues or published-result searches. Those two natural missing solids supply a genuine whole-family completion; the other three sample counts are mechanical consequences of already known second moments and are not treated as new. Best-of-knowledge PASS retains archival risks rather than equating failed searches with novelty.

value.rationale: The scale-invariant random-shadow-area variance is a natural uncertainty invariant for Cauchy surface-area estimation. The complete five-member Platonic comparison is a motivated finite natural classification: dodecahedron and icosahedron introduce genuinely new golden-ratio angular correlations and supply two exact missing second moments, precise rank and RMS sample budgets. The partial older three-solid table, known kernel and purely algebraic k=ceil(10000 V) consequences are not credited as separate contributions. No arbitrary slices or unsupported broader theorems are needed.
residual_risks: The practical cutoffs are exact only for independent uniform directions and RMS, not confidence bounds.
Originality of the two remaining rows is conditional on bounded literature comparison; archival sources remain inaccessible.

final_claim: For every regular Euclidean Platonic solid, normalized variance Var(area(P projected onto U^perp))/(S(P)/4)^2 for uniform U on S² equals 16/(9π)-5/9 (cube), (4sqrt2+2asin(1/3))/(3π)-2/3 (tetrahedron and octahedron), 20(2+asin(1/sqrt5))/(9πsqrt5)-7/9 (dodecahedron), and (16sqrt2+8+8asin(1/3)+4sqrt5 asin(sqrt5/3))/(15π)-13/15 (icosahedron); the values strictly decrease in the stated order and independent-uniform-view 1%-relative-RMS surface-area estimation requires exactly 104,57,57,16,6 views, respectively.
limitations: The three tetrahedron/cube/octahedron values are previously given by Finch 2012, not novel on their own.
Priority of dodecahedron/icosahedron exact second moments remains best-of-knowledge with inaccessible earlier papers.
Independent uniform samples and RMS error only; no high-probability confidence conclusion.
